items.period: Shang oracle-script style; the file page points to Sinica record 43.F555, 合137 賓組
items.tradition: Oracle-bone script style; modern vector reconstruction
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction of 六 in Shang oracle-script style, associated by its source page with Sinica record 43.F555. The early graph is attested in numeral uses, while its original graphic explanation remains disputed.
items.alt: Black reconstructed oracle-script glyph for 六 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows an early script-style candidate relevant to the inscriptional numeral attestations while leaving the shelter and 入-related analyses unresolved.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page; attribution appreciated.

items.tradition: Bronze script style; modern vector reconstruction
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction labelled Western Zhou bronze-script style, offering a later comparison with the Shang-style form. It illustrates a script tradition and does not resolve the competing origin proposals.
items.alt: Black reconstructed bronze-script glyph for 六 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Adds a later labelled script-style comparison without asserting a continuous, fully documented transformation.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page; attribution appreciated.

limitations.text: The image URLs use Wikimedia Commons’ Special:Redirect/file endpoint, which could not itself be opened by the web tool. The corresponding file-description pages were opened and provide the direct-file links, source descriptions, and reuse statements.

The selected glyphs are digital reconstructions, not artifact photographs. The oracle candidate’s source description cites a particular Sinica record, but the underlying record image was not independently inspected in this run.
